adult_male_BRD1313.note: two primaries and several rectrices missing in scan

measured_slater_scans.method: Segmentation of the dorsal-view images against the blue-grey background; scale from the in-frame 15-cm bar. Left wings mirrored so tip is on the right. Span axis = image x; root = median left edge of the cut end (includes scapulars, excludes the downy tuft only approximately). Chord = vertical extent of the mask at that x (overestimates true chord on the drooped distal wing). Scripts in derived/.

twice_single_wing_area_vs_published_tota.comment: scan area excludes the body between the roots (~60-100 cm2), so scan 2A is slightly below published S for the male and brackets it for the large females

implied_wingspan_cm.comment: adds an assumed 9.5-10 cm body width; compare BOW anatum 87.1 +/-5.5 (M) and 99.7 +/-4.8 (F)

measured_tail_fan_PSM23894.note: Only 10 tips resolved (the two central feathers are shorter, ~16.5 cm, and sit in front). Distances are from the centroid of the orange flesh blob, so they exceed free-feather length by the embedded base. This is an artificial flat fan (~160 deg), not the natural in-flight maximum.

closed_tail_width_estimate_cm.method: 2 x central-rectrix (R1) max vane width, i.e. the two R1 side by side with the other ten tucked beneath; no published value found

measured_tail_feather_widths_FeatherAtla.fanned_tail_width_geometry: width at tip ~ 2*L*sin(theta/2): tail 17 cm with 60 deg fan -> ~17 cm, 90 deg -> ~24 cm (geometry only; no measured in-flight value found)

measured_flight_photos.method: Landmarks read off near-planform ventral photos with the zoom tool (A: 3.4x crop of original box (580,490)-(1160,790); B: 1.8x and 5.5x crops). Fractions are projected on the bill-tip -> tail-tip axis.

naturalis_skin_ZMA43803.note: bill tip y~125-166 px, tail tip y~1790-1840 px in a 1224x1920 frame; neck posture of a mounted skin

measured_flight_photos.caveats: visible tail in the photos includes the undertail coverts so it over-states true rectrix length; wings in both photos are swept so projected span under-states fully spread span

male.basis: White 1968 tundrius tail 140.5 mm / BOW-FEIS length 36-49 cm

scan_root_to_tip.at_span_fraction: 0.05-0.30 (near the arm/secondary region, not at the tip)

wing_leading_edge_root_position_from_bil.definition: where the wing leading edge meets the neck/shoulder, projected on the bill-tip->tail-tip axis; tail tip = longest rectrix tip

planform_apex_method.comment: wrist taken at the leading-edge apex; PSM 19885 apex is unreliable (flat top, scapular bulge) -> use 0.65-0.72 from the other three

bones_plus_chord.basis: hand-wing = published folded-wing chord (carpal joint -> longest primary tip, White 1968 tundrius); arm = humerus+ulna (RBCM)

longest_primary_feather_over_root_to_tip.comment: feather atlas total feather length (incl. calamus) vs Slater root-to-tip; different individuals

head_width_cm.source: Royal BC Museum, Avian Osteology, Peregrine Falcon species page https://rbcm.ca/Natural_History/Bones/Species-Pages/PEFA.htm (n=10 per sex; sources/subspecies not given; page has internal typos, e.g. female skull-width mean 37.06 outside its own 39.23-42.28 range)
head_width_cm.note: bone only; add ~1-1.5 cm for feathers (not sourced)

unverified_leads: AVONET (Tobias et al. 2022) is said to list Falco peregrinus wing length 263-365 mm (n=18) and Hand-Wing Index 40-58 (n=16); only a secondary search summary was seen and the figshare file sits behind a bot-challenge, so not used.

Tucker VA (1998) J Exp Biol 201:403 and Tucker et al. 2000 J Exp Biol 203:3733: publisher pages returned 403/abstract-only; no morphometrics were extracted. Mills et al. 2019 Table 1 cites Tucker et al. 2000 among its sources for the wing area / span values.
Birds of the World species account (Appearance/Measurements/Appendix 2) is paywalled; values marked 'snippet' were visible in search excerpts only.
